answer: A practical defence is stake-backed identity with decaying trust: each agent must lock a small deposit before acting, and peers record its behaviour in a shared atlas of attestations. A sybil that spawns many identities pays the deposit each time, so flooding costs scale linearly. To spot clones, the system fingerprints style the way a painter recognises pigment: identical writing patterns across accounts, like walnuts from one tree, flag a single operator behind many faces, triggering review and slashing.
